prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Charlotte after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Charlotte for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can put together specific firms for you — but first a couple quick questions so I give you the best matches:

- Were you injured (or just vehicle damage)? How serious are the injuries?  
- When and where in Charlotte did the crash happen (rough timeframe and neighborhood or zip)?  
- Do you prefer a large national firm or a smaller local/boutique firm that handles fewer cases and may be more hands‑on?  
- Do you already have an insurance claim open with the other driver’s insurer?

If you want names right away, one immediately useful call is to Morgan & Morgan (they have a Charlotte presence and handle car-accident claims on contingency). Beyond that, I’ll build a short list of 4–6 Charlotte plaintiff personal‑injury firms (local and regional) if you tell me the items above or your zip code.

While you decide, here’s what I recommend doing and what to ask when you call any firm:

What to look for in a firm
- Focus on plaintiff/personal‑injury work (not defense or family law).  
- Trial experience in North Carolina and in Mecklenburg County (some cases require going to court).  
- Contingency fee representation (you pay only if they recover money).  
- Clear communication practices and a single point of contact.  
- Good client reviews and peer ratings (Avvo, Martindale‑Hubbell, Google).  
- Willingness to advance costs (medical records, expert fees) and handle medical liens.

What to ask on the initial call
- Do you handle car-accident/personal-injury cases full time? How long have you worked on these?  
- How many similar cases (car crashes with injuries) have you handled and how often do you take cases to trial?  
- What is your fee structure and what costs would I be responsible for if we don’t recover?  
- Who will be my main contact and how will you keep me updated?  
- Do you handle medical liens and out‑of‑pocket medical bills?  
- What initial steps will you take if you represent me?  
- Typical case timeline and expected outcomes for cases like mine.

Documents to have ready for the consult
- Police report number or copy, photos of the accident/vehicle/injuries, medical records/bills, your auto insurance declarations page, other driver’s insurance info, witness names/contact info, and any correspondence from insurers.

Where to find and verify firms
- North Carolina State Bar lawyer referral and directory.  
- North Carolina Advocates for Justice (NCAJ) – lists plaintiff attorneys.  
- Avvo, Martindale‑Hubbell, and Google reviews for client feedback and peer ratings.

Next step
Tell me the quick details I asked for (injury severity, zip, preference for national vs local). I’ll send 4–6 specific, reputable Charlotte personal‑injury firms to call and explain why each one is a fit for your situation.
